land.text: Lérida, taken from the Banu Tujib wālīs in 1039 together with Zaragoza by al-Musta'in of the Banu Hud and given to a younger son

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Taifa of Zaragoza shapes of 1040-1110 contain Lleida; this dossier carves it out.

land.text: Lérida, which 'appears to have fallen to the Almoravids' in 1102 (others: 1110)

successors.note: The Almoravids held it through wālīs until the Catalans took it in 1149 (Lleida page).

capitals.name: Lérida (Lleida)
capitals.note: The page calls Lérida the basis of the taifa; Barbastro was its second city until 1100.

rulers.name: Yusuf al-Muzaffar ibn Sulayman ibn Hud
rulers.note: Page: 1039/1046 to 1078/1081. Younger son of al-Musta'in; the elder, Ahmad al-Muqtadir, inherited Zaragoza in 1046.

rulers.name: al-Mundhir (al-Hajib)
rulers.note: Inherited Lérida in late 1081; already governed Denia and Tortosa as his father's hājib.

correction.text: Lérida with its district and Barbastro, 'the second city of the ṭāʾifa'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Lérida row and its Zaragoza shapes 1040-1084 (36.4-38.0 thousand km2) contain these lands. The page names Lérida and Barbastro and, by the later conquests, Graus, Estada, Monzón, Almenar, Sariñena, Pomar de Cinca and Albalate de Cinca; two circles of 45 km are the reading. The Zaragoza page gives the separation as c. 1040, this page as 1039/1046. No infobox area on either page.

correction.text: as before without Graus, taken in 1083

keyframe_review.note: Graus (1083). Estada, Monzón and Almenar follow between 1087 and 1093.

correction.text: without Graus, Estada, Monzón and Almenar, all taken by the Aragonese by 1093

keyframe_review.note: Barbastro, Sariñena and the lower Cinca are still Lérida's until 1100-1101.

correction.text: without Barbastro and Sariñena, captured in 1100

keyframe_review.note: One year: the Cinca valley south of Monzón falls in 1101.

correction.text: a rump around Lérida after Pomar de Cinca and Albalate de Cinca fell in 1101, 'bringing the Aragonese up to Lérida itself'

keyframe_review.note: To the Almoravid conquest of 1102 (some sources 1110).

region.text: Lérida and Barbastro, the lands of the younger Hudid son

ledger.note: c. 1040: Lérida becomes a separate taifa under Yusuf, a son of al-Musta'in of the Banu Hud. 'Between c. 1040 and c. 1105, the Taifa of Lérida was separate from that of Zaragoza.' The Lleida page: taken from the Banu Tujib with Zaragoza in 1039; ruler Yusuf from 1039/1046; in 1046 'the elder son, Aḥmad al-Muḳtadir, inherited Zaragoza'. The extent is a reading of the later conquests.

1078: civil war between the brothers Yusuf of Lérida and al-Muqtadir of Zaragoza, which 'reunited' the Hudid principality under al-Muqtadir by 1081 (page paraphrase: 1078-81). The page does not say who held Lérida at any date within it.
1081: the civil war ends with al-Muqtadir master of the whole principality; 'When al-Muḳtadir died in late 1081, the ṭāʾifa was divided between his two sons.'

late 1081: al-Mundhir inherits Lérida at the division of al-Muqtadir's realm: 'The younger, al-Mundhir, who was already governing Denia and Tortosa as his father's ḥājib, inherited Lérida also.' The Zaragoza dossier books no matching loss.

region.text: Tortosa, governed by al-Mundhir as hājib

ledger.note: 1081: al-Mundhir holds Tortosa with Lérida (a governorship, drawn as the dependent tint). Cliopatria has no Tortosa shape for 1066-1084; the 1085 shape is used.

region.text: Denia, governed by al-Mundhir as hājib

ledger.note: 1081: al-Mundhir holds Denia with Lérida; the page has al-Muqtadir acquire Denia in 1076 and Tortosa in 1061.
1083: Graus falls: 'In 1083, they took Graus' (the passage does not name 'they'; read as the Aragonese, since Peter of Aragon takes the next towns).

1090: al-Mundhir dies and his minor son Sulayman succeeds; 'Sulaymān's regents divided the ṭāʾifa, separating Denia and Tortosa to their own advantage and leaving him a rump Lérida.' The year is the succession's; the page does not date the separation.
1090: Denia separated from Lérida by Sulayman's regents (see Tortosa).
by 1093: 'between 1087 and 1093, Peter took Estada, Monzón and Almenar' (Peter, 'now king of Aragon' by 1100); dated at the end of the span.
1100: 'Peter, now king of Aragon, captured Barbastro, the second city of the ṭāʾifa, and Sariñena.'

region.text: Pomar de Cinca and Albalate de Cinca, the Cinca valley as far as Lérida

ledger.note: 1101: 'the capture of Pomar de Cinca and Albalate de Cinca brought the Aragonese up to Lérida itself.'

1102: Lérida 'appears to have fallen to the Almoravids that year, although others have it lasting until 1110'; the Zaragoza page has the separation end c. 1105. Ermengol V of Urgell died fighting the Almoravids at Mollerussa in September 1102.
1102: the Taifa of Lérida ends; the Almoravids 'appointed wālīs to govern it until it was captured by the Catalans in 1149'.

wars.name: Hudid civil war of 1078-1081
wars.outcome: The brothers' war reunited the Hudid principality under al-Muqtadir; on his death in late 1081 it was divided again and al-Mundhir took Lérida.
wars.note: The page gives only the years; no battle is named.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of the Cinca valley and Barbastro

zones.text: Graus 1083; Estada, Monzón, Almenar 1087-93; Barbastro and Sariñena 1100; Pomar and Albalate de Cinca 1101

wars.outcome: The Aragonese took the taifa's northern and eastern towns one by one and reached Lérida by 1101; Ermengol IV of Urgell attacked toward Balaguer in 1089, 'possibly taking it briefly'.
wars.note: Parias were paid to Barcelona from 1045 and later to Barcelona and Urgell (page); no territorial change.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of Lérida
wars.outcome: Lérida fell to the Almoravids in 1102 (others: 1110) after Ermengol V of Urgell's defeat at Mollerussa.

certainty.note: The pages name towns and no boundaries; the extent is a reading of the later conquests. The frontier with Aragon is sharper only in the sense that the towns lost are dated (1083-1101).

notes: Written for eu-12-x (states Cliopatria lacks; requested by eu-12-h as taifa-of-lerida); two pages (Lleida twice). Cliopatria has no Lérida row: the Zaragoza shapes of 1040-1110 contain Lleida and Barbastro, which the Zaragoza dossier already books as a c. 1040 loss and a 1078-1081 contest with this slug. Start 1040 follows the Zaragoza page (the Lleida page: 1039/1046); end 1102 follows the Lleida page (it says 1102/1110; the Zaragoza page c. 1105; the Zaragoza dossier ends Zaragoza in 1110). The Almoravids held Lérida by wālīs to 1149, when the Catalans captured it (county-of-barcelona and county-of-urgell dossiers should carry that; this dossier ends before it). Parias were paid to Barcelona from 1045: a vassal_start for Lleida belongs in the county-of-barcelona dossier (not opened here). Not settled: who held Lérida between the war's end and late 1081; the page names no boundary, so every extent is a reading (two 45 km circles); the Tujibid wālīs before 1039 need a dossier (tujibids-of-zaragoza was already suggested by eu-12-a). Gazetteer names needed: Lleida, Barbastro, Graus, Monzón, Almenar, Sariñena (places; Natural Earth has only the province Lérida).
